post.originalText:
COMPETITION 10: Battle of Waterloo

Who do you think represented the battle best? 

__

Live 3D Voxel Diorama w/ Destructible Buildings.

Same prompt across 4 frontier models in Command Code: build a moving 3D voxel diorama of the Battle of Waterloo with cannons firing and destroying buildings. Each had the goal of representing the Battle in the most detail possible. 

I do not want to judge for you which won... Who do you think won? 

__

1. Gemini 4 Argon (High): 16m 00s, 105k out tokens (8.13M in), ~$3.21.
By far the largest and most complete battlefield: 64,530 voxels, 1,132 articulated soldiers, 20 cannons firing salvos that blast craters and fire into Château d'Hougoumont and La Haye Sainte, the Charge of the Royal Scots Greys, Napoleon's Grand Battery, Plancenoit Church, and 6 interactive historical phases with smooth close-up camera flights. Is it the best looking however? Does it look the most accurate? 

2. Claude Opus 5.5: 11m 07s, 65.8k out tokens (327k in), ~$1.85.
Best lighting and atmosphere out of the box. Warm golden-hour sun on a wooden plinth with a brass "Bataille de Waterloo" plaque. Features true flood-fill structural collapse when cannonballs cut a wall or tower off from the ground, bouncing roundshot, a Ball Cam that rides the cannonball into the building, and Hougoumont burning. (Note: on max effort it initially spent 2h 34m / 830k out tokens / ~$19.89 over-thinking Three.js internals before timing out; once capped so it actually wrote the file, it finished in 11m 07s for $1.85.)

3. Muse Wonder 1.0 (xHigh): 9m 05s, 62.5k out tokens (3.68M in), ~$3.78.
The fastest model to finish a full multi-phase battle from scratch. Great dawn-to-dusk mood, firing artillery salvos, collapsing walls at La Haye Sainte, a live 2D tactical field-map radar, and dedicated landmark cameras (Hougoumont, Wellington's Ridge, Grand Battery, Plancenoit). Does not look half bad but is number 4 for me. 

4. GPT-6.1 Sol (Max): 21m 48s, 27.1k out tokens (4.05M in), ~$0.98.
Best bang for your buck under $1. Clean, polished museum tabletop presentation with 888 articulated figures, Ney's Cuirassiers, British infantry squares, firing cannons, and destructible masonry — just a bit more compact and understated in scale compared to the top three. Honestly, this one looks the most like the actual battlefield rather than Voxel. Very cool. 

__

Which model do you think won the Battle of Waterloo competition?

sourceMaterials.text: @dextune I lowkey like 6.1 Sol best for this one. Maybe cause it looks like a real model diorama
